description:
An open-source visual workspace for building with Claude Code and Codex.

Nimbalyst is a free, open-source, local visual workspace for building with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. It combines WYSIWYG editors for markdown, mockups, Mermaid, Excalidraw, CSV, data models, and code with parallel session management, task tracking, and git tooling.
Features include visual editors where humans and coding agents collaborate on the same files, a kanban-style session manager that links files to sessions, task and bug tracking, AI-assisted commits, worktrees, an embedded terminal, a mobile companion app, and a pluggable extension system for custom editors.
August 22nd, 2026 Release
A recovery update for anyone whose sessions disappeared.
If your session list came up empty
Some installs could start up on a brand-new, empty database while the real one — every session, every conversation, all of your document history — sat untouched on disk beside it. The app looked completely normal, because your project list is stored separately. Only the sessions were missing.
Nothing was deleted. This update detects that situation at startup and opens the database that actually holds your data. If you were affected, install this release and your sessions come back on the next launch. There is nothing to restore by hand.
If your sessions are still missing after updating, please open an issue and include your startup log — the two causes behind this symptom need different recovery steps, and the log says which one you hit.
Fixed
- Installs that came up with an empty database now open the one that actually holds their sessions.
- The database restore guide now identifies which database an install is using before recommending a backup, so a recovery step cannot overwrite good data with an empty copy.
